analysis: This PR changes only documentation: docs/architecture/scheduling.md (shown in head text only) and docs/provider/cli-reference.md (a timestamp bump plus a new paragraph on the catalog picker's shared activation reserve). No executable code, wire protocol, authorization, attestation, encryption, billing or revocation logic changes. The new text states that picker estimates are nominal and that live admission (configured reserve, current available memory) still applies, so no admission or serving-trust control is weakened. The docs also keep the existing statements that warm-pool eligibility uses the same complete legacy or App Attest serving policy as dispatch (scheduling.md lines 127-130) and that App Attest never changes capacity or grants legacy trust flags. These reaffirm TB-011/T-052/T-053 and do not alter them. The scheduling.md patch shows no diff, so its exact edits cannot be isolated from the head text. I found nothing in the visible text that invalidates a threat-model assumption. Doc claims about code symbols (Start.pickerSelectionFitsBudget, PickerReserveMode, etc.) are unverifiable here because the source was not supplied. Memory-availability modes are a resource-admission concern and do not touch the T-016/T-029 security conclusions as written. No new attack surface or threat-model update is needed.
